images.caption:
At the end of Fazeley Street (at the junction with Floodgate Street) is Fazeley Studios.
It is at 191 Fazeley Street.
It is the home of Ikon Eastside.

The building on the corner with Floodgate Street was the Unitarian Sunday School of 1865 by A B Phipson, extended to the street corner in 1868.
History
Fazeley Studios might be a 21st century creative community, but architecturally, the building dates back nearly 150 years to when Digbeth was a gritty industrial and commercial centre. We've done all we can to preserve this heritage, maintaining a strong sense of continuity with the past.
The grand central reception was formerly a Unitarian Chapel designed by George Ingall and opened in 1876.
The oldest part of the building was constructed as a Unitarian Sunday school in 1865, and now houses a spacious conference room and a group of character studios.
The north light studios occupy a series of factory buildings dating from the 1920s.
Digbeth was first settled in the 6th century and became an important centre for industry in medieval times as local rivers were harnessed to power its mills, before playing its part in the industrial revolution. In the 21st century, the area's excellent accessibility, facilities and affordability are promoting it as the Creative and Digital capital of the region.

Fazeley Studios was conceived in 2006, and with the support of Advantage West Midlands has been the subject of a comprehensive reconstruction.

images.caption: Vee have vays of making you enjoy zee exhibition! The former board school in what is now Ouzel Square has been transformed into the Ikon Gallery.  This runs a wide range of exhibitions of modern art.  One of the current "installations" involves strapping visitors to a board and sliding them out of this 2nd floor window as seen in the picture.  Although they are sometimes pushed further out than seen here, they do get to be pulled back inside again afterwards!

images.caption: Ouzell Square Although sandwiched between the bustling Brindley Place and the traffic in Broad Street, this square is a haven of tranquility in the centre of Birmingham.  The garden in the middle is in the Japanese tradition with a water feature and gravel that is regularly raked. At the far end of the Ouzell Square, in the next grid square is the former Board School, now renovated and housing the Ikon Gallery showing exhibitions of contemporary art.
